subject: Observability delivery & pipeline assimilation for ACME private deployment
messages:
From: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@acme-sec.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-sec.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability requirements for private deployment (attached)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the intake call last week. I've attached our observability requirements (acme-obsv-requirements.pdf) to give more color on what we need from the private deployment:

- Secure, auditable delivery of logs to our Splunk instance (HEC) and a long-term S3 archive for audit evidence.
- Tracing hooks that preserve W3C trace context across the inference runtime and customer-facing proxies.
- Ability to route high-frequency metrics to our Prometheus-compatible endpoint while keeping high-cardinality traces sampled for cost.
- End-to-end evidence chain (who accessed what, when) for SOC2 auditors.

Questions that would help our procurement and network teams:
1) What connector modes do you support for on-prem/private? (syslog over TLS, Splunk HEC, S3 sink, forwarder sidecar, direct push)
2) Do you support mutual TLS for HEC and how are tokens stored/rotated?
3) What IP ranges/outbound ports do we need to open from our VPC to allow the data plane to send telemetry?

Can we get a short proposed delivery plan and a list of artifacts you’ll need from our side (diagram, egress IPs, test index, sample logs)? I’d like to schedule a 30-min technical coupling next week if that works.

Appreciate it,
Jordan
Jordan Matthews
Head of Infrastructure Security
ACME Security

(attachment: acme-obsv-requirements.pdf - 1.2MB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@acme-sec.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-sec.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability requirements for private deployment (attached)

Jordan — thanks for the detailed doc and the clear asks. High level we can support the flows you describe; below is a pragmatic delivery approach and a short list of inputs we’ll need.

Summary plan (3 phases):

1) Discovery & gating (1 week):
- Confirm architecture diagram, test VPC, egress proxy details, and an index for Splunk HEC.
- Validate compliance requirements: retention windows, encryption-at-rest, access audit expectations.

2) Integration adapters (2–3 weeks):
- Forwarder sidecar (Fluent Bit / Fluentd) deployed adjacent to the inference pods for log batching + TLS syslog forwarding OR
- Splunk HEC ingestion via mTLS (preferred for high-throughput tokenized events); we can also stage to S3 with signed URLs for long-term retention.
- Metrics: Prometheus remote_write or Pushgateway for meter-level metrics; we’ll provide a Prometheus scrape/exporter pattern if you prefer pull.
- Tracing: use OpenTelemetry collector as the standard in-cluster adapter. We’ll preserve W3C traceparent and provide a sampling policy hook so your SEA/Prod tracing costs stay controlled.

3) Acceptance & evidence handoff (1 week):
- Runbook-based verification of sample events, trace correlation checks, and an evidence packet (signed manifest + log hash) for SOC2.

Inputs we need from ACME:
- Architecture diagram with NAT/egress proxies and any proxy TLS interception
- Egress IPs you’ll open (or confirmation you’ll use an egress proxy we should hit)
- Splunk HEC endpoint(s) + preferred auth (mTLS / token)
- A test index and ingestion quota for validation

Security & custody notes:
- We recommend mTLS for HEC where possible; when tokens are used we store them in a local KMS-backed secret and rotate via our provisioning pipeline.
- Evidence handshake: we provide a signed manifest (SHA256 bundle) at acceptance with signer identity and timestamp to satisfy audit chains.

I’m looping in Kimberly (engineering) on the CC so she can add specifics on keys, ports, and sampling knobs. Can we lock a 30-min timeslot next Tue or Wed?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observability requirements for private deployment (technical checklist)

Jordan / Soojin — a few concrete constraints and recommendations from the infra side so the integration is smooth:

Checklist (technical):
- Network / Ports: outbound 443 (HEC mTLS) and 9443 (OTel collector endpoint) are sufficient if you route through your egress proxy. If you require direct host IPs, we’ll provide a /24 range for the cluster egress.
- mTLS & certs: we support client certs for HEC; certs can be rotated via ACME or you can provision certs and we’ll mount them into the forwarder sidecar.
- Token storage: HEC tokens must be stored in KMS; we will not persist plaintext tokens on disk. Rotation window: recommend 7–14 days with auto-rotation hooks.
- Batching & backpressure: forwarder defaults are 5s/1MB flush; for high-volume workloads we recommend 1s/4MB for logs and larger batch sizes on the S3 staging path to reduce calls.
- Tracing hooks: maintain W3C traceparent. We’ll instrument internal request boundaries and expose a sampling configuration endpoint so you can switch sampling rates without a redeploy. For service-to-service trace propagation across the inference runtime and any customer-side proxy, we recommend header passthrough and sticky-sampling at the edge.
- Evidence chain: each acceptance run will produce an evidence manifest (manifest.json) and a signed SHA256 bundle. We’ll provide a short script that pushes the bundle to your S3 archive and logs the transfer in our audit index.

Pre-prod request: provide a test Splunk HEC token/index and a small test stream (50–200 events/min) so we can validate header sanitization, timestamp fidelity, and event ordering under load.

Operational links we’ll use:
- Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/ACME+Onboarding
- Playbook for cert rotation: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/Cert+Rotation

I’ll also attach a short matrix of sink options in the next message for your security team to sign-off.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
